title: Göreme Open Air Museum, Zelve & Paşabağ: Ticket & Timing Guide
seoTitle: Göreme Open Air Museum, Zelve & Paşabağ: 2026 Ticket Guide
metaDescription: Plan your visit to Göreme Open Air Museum, the Dark Church, Zelve, and Paşabağ. Verified 2026 euro fees, MuseumPass math, and bus-free arrival times.
quickAnswer: In 2026, foreign-visitor entry costs €20 for [Göreme Open Air Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=GRM01&DistId=GRM), €6 extra for the [Dark Church](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-GRM02-01-009), and €12 for the combined [Zelve–Paşabağ](https://muze.gov.tr/ETicket) ticket. Arrive at Göreme right at 08:00 or after 15:30 to miss tour-bus queues, and always buy the Dark Church add-on.

body.text: Is the Dark Church extra ticket worth buying?

Yes—the €6 extra ticket for the Dark Church (Karanlık Kilise) is the single highest-value add-on in Cappadocia. Because only one tiny narthex window admits sunlight, its 11th-century New Testament frescoes avoided centuries of UV fading and preserve deep lapis blues, ochres, and gold highlights unmatched anywhere else in the complex.

Other chapels inside [Göreme Open Air Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=GRM01&DistId=GRM)—such as Elmali (Apple), Yılanlı (Snake), and St. Barbara—suffer from scratched faces and sun damage. Inside the Dark Church, scenes of Christ Pantocrator, the Last Supper, and the Betrayal of Judas read almost like illuminated manuscripts. Photography is strictly banned inside to protect the pigments, and staff cap interior capacity, so buy the €6 ticket at the main gate (or online via [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-GRM02-01-009)) rather than walking back from the chapel door.

Do not skip Tokalı (Buckle) Church either: it sits 50 meters downhill outside the main exit gate, is included in your €20 main ticket, and houses the largest painted Byzantine interior in the Göreme valley.
What is the difference between Göreme Open Air Museum and Zelve?

Göreme Open Air Museum is a compact, UNESCO-listed monastic complex inscribed in 1985 ([UNESCO World Heritage Centre](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/357/)) prized for painted Byzantine churches, whereas Zelve is a sprawling three-valley abandoned troglodyte village inhabited until 1952. Paşabağ (Monks Valley), bundled on Zelve's €12 ticket, showcases Cappadocia's tallest multi-capped fairy chimneys.

body.text: If you only have energy for one open-air site on a tight schedule, choose Göreme for art history and frescoes, or Zelve–Paşabağ for raw scale, wandering room, and iconic fairy chimneys. On a [3-day Cappadocia itinerary](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/3-days-in-cappadocia), seeing Göreme at 08:00 and Zelve–Paşabağ in the late afternoon pairs effortlessly.

Enter Göreme Open Air Museum at opening time (08:00) or after 15:30 to avoid the 09:45–14:30 Red Tour coach wave. Between 10:00 and 13:30, bottlenecks form outside every tiny chapel doorway—especially Elmali and the Dark Church—turning a 90-minute visit into a slow queue under direct sun.
Practical timing tactics that work year-round:

items: Go straight to the Dark Church first: If you enter at 08:00, walk directly to the upper terrace for the Dark Church before day-tour buses finish parking, then loop back to the lower chapels.
Visit Tokalı Church at midday: Even when the main loop is packed, Tokalı Church across the road rarely has a line because rushed tour groups often skip it.
Save Zelve–Paşabağ for 16:00 onward: Late-afternoon raking light brings out the texture of Paşabağ's mushroom-capped chimneys and cools Zelve's three canyons down after midday heat.

body.text: Does MuseumPass Türkiye cover Cappadocia sites?

Yes—the 15-day [MuseumPass Türkiye](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009) (€165 in 2026) covers more than 350 Ministry of Culture and Tourism sites nationwide, including Göreme Open Air Museum, Zelve–Paşabağ, Derinkuyu, Kaymaklı, and Ihlara Valley. However, neither MuseumPass Türkiye nor the 3-day €65 [MuseumPass Cappadocia](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Furun-detay%3FCatalogNo%3DKRT-MSP01-19-001) covers the €6 Dark Church.

Do the math before buying a pass. If Cappadocia is your only archaeological stop in Türkiye, the core four sites (Göreme €20 + Zelve–Paşabağ €12 + one underground city €13 + Ihlara Valley €15) total €60—making single e-tickets cheaper than the €65 regional pass. By contrast, if your 10–14 day trip also includes Ephesus (€40), Pamukkale (€30), and major Istanbul state museums, the €165 nationwide pass pays for itself quickly and skips ticket-desk lines (each pass allows one entry per site). For southern-corridor planning, compare underground sites in our [Derinkuyu vs Kaymaklı guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/derinkuyu-vs-kaymakli).

faq.q: Can I buy Göreme Open Air Museum tickets online in advance?
faq.a: Yes. Official foreign-visitor e-tickets and MuseumPasses are sold directly through the Ministry of Culture and Tourism portal at [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/ETicket). Avoid third-party reseller sites that mark up standard €20 tickets with "skip-the-line" surcharges.

faq.q: Are Zelve and Paşabağ on the same ticket in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. The Ministry issues a single combined Zelve–Paşabağlar ticket for €12 in 2026. Keep your ticket barcode after visiting Paşabağ so you can scan into Zelve Open Air Museum (about 1.5 km away) on the same day.

faq.q: Is photography allowed inside Göreme Open Air Museum churches?
faq.a: Outdoor photography of the rock facades and valleys is allowed, but flash photography—and in the Dark Church and Tokalı Church, all photography—is prohibited inside painted chapels to prevent pigment degradation.

faq.q: How far is Göreme Open Air Museum from Göreme town center?
faq.a: It sits roughly 1.5 km (about a 20-minute uphill walk) east of central Göreme along a paved sidewalk. Taxis take five minutes from town if you want to save your legs for afternoon valley hikes.

faq.q: What are the opening hours for Göreme Open Air Museum?
faq.a: Opening hours run seasonally—typically 08:00 to 19:00 or 20:00 in peak summer and 08:00 to 17:00 in winter, with ticket sales closing 30–45 minutes before closing. Always verify exact seasonal hours on muze.gov.tr the day before.

faq.q: Can you visit both Göreme Open Air Museum and Zelve on the same day?
faq.a: Yes, and they complement each other well. Visit Göreme at 08:00 while the frescoed chapels are quiet, break for lunch and a rest during midday heat, then visit Paşabağ and Zelve after 15:30.
